Replay

Replay Speedball

11 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Authored rules and deliberate differencesPrediction and presentationSession/UI acceptanceNative host migrationPlay again and local profilesSave and resume a pitchBrowser partiesBrowser solo save slots

A separate Speedball port using a complete, replayable pitch. Every playable peer predicts all players and the shared ball before the authority settles their state. Replay's runner schedules the simulation steps and manages input and history. Contacts, kicks, spikes, score and kickoff state live in ordinary Odin values in shared/pitch; the Godot script handles input and views. Original Speedball, Claimball and Slopball remain independently runnable.

From the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/play.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_speedball/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/network_run.sh

The interactive default is a menu with Solo, Host, Join and Watch. Set the name, address and port there; the host starts a manually opened pitch. For scripted automatic launches in two windows:

Shell
RSB_ROLE=host nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/play.sh
RSB_ROLE=client nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/play.sh

WASD moves, Space holds kick, E spikes, Tab holds scores and Enter focuses chat. Escape returns the keyboard from chat. Typing captures gameplay controls. The scoreboard shows names, teams and round-trip telemetry, retaining departed rows. Leave returns to the menu and clears the local session; rejoining an existing match uses the current authoritative state. Roles are solo, host, server (no avatar) and client/observer. Default port is 49480; RSB_PORT overrides it. RSB_PLAYERS sets the start threshold; RSB_GOALS sets the winning score. RSB_TOKEN labels deterministic test credentials and bypasses local profiles. Without it, native/browser play persists a random reconnect identity and the chosen name; see the profile section below. The menu supports a direct address; RSB_ADDRESS supplies its default. Configure RSB_ROOM_SERVICE for the party create/invite/rejoin menu. The default direct mode does not provide automatic matchmaking or a public service. RSB_BOT=striker chases/kicks, spiker performs a two-command burst, and other nonempty bot labels idle. RSB_LATENCY/RSB_JITTER are milliseconds; RSB_LOSS/RSB_DUPLICATE are ten-thousandths. Set REPLAY_KEEP_LOGS=1 to retain network gate logs. Native macOS gameplay is tested; the WASM gate type-checks the pure simulation. The separate browser gate below establishes browser party multiplayer; deterministic P2P remains a separate runner/gate.

Authored rules and deliberate differences#

The port preserves the 640×360 pitch, wall/goal geometry, 9/8-pixel player/ball radii, player speed 2.2 and momentum response 0.35, kick reach/power/cooldown, spike reach/power, soft dribble contact, ball friction/speed cap/restitution, 72-tick kickoff hold, and goal detection from the previous clamped ball position. Dedicated seat numbering has a one-seat offset to retain original spawn/team assignment: the first client scores into the left goal. Scene provenance is in assets.md.

Unlike the original mixed simulation/discrete fields, the complete score and winner participate in replay with the ball. The HUD reads authoritative score; goal reset/hold predict immediately. A changed reset counter cuts smoothing. The new runner processes contacts in explicit ascending seat order.

Spike commands carry intent, and both authority and prediction derive the origin from the issuing seat's world position. The original command accepts issuer-supplied coordinates. This is a deliberate trust-model change, not equivalent command validation. Replay currently services one reliable action per seat per tick, so the two commands execute on successive ticks. The spiker bot requests its burst within 30 pixels, leaving room inside the 44-pixel predicate for both to be valid. The original bot requests within 44 pixels and supplies its captured coordinates. These differences must be accounted for in a paired benchmark.

The HUD/team colors remain a separate implementation. Direct session menus, chat and held scores are now supplied and tested. Public deployment, Steam paths and broader visual/human play-feel review remain pending. The port ledger records what is preserved and what remains. The native Room path described below now exercises migration in this pitch. This remains an incomplete M6 port, not full game parity.

Prediction and presentation#

Presentation selects the state and effects to display. Its smoothing changes the drawn pose while the simulation retains the values used for gameplay.

The runner now refreshes remote held-input guesses from each authoritative snapshot before replaying the speculative suffix. Local input samples, aiming stamps and action IDs stay unchanged. The replacement inputs and resulting state/events commit atomically; a failed replay preserves the old timeline.

client.correction contains detached before/after frames at the same prediction tick, an authority tick and replay depth. The view feeds their position difference to view.smooth_correct, then advances ordinary presentation normally. This avoids smoothing away legitimate movement. Corrections beyond 60 pixels and goal resets cut the glide. Smoothing never changes gameplay or checksums.

Playable peers use speculative kick flashes on the complete predicted pitch; incorrect flashes can be canceled/replaced. RSB_RESULT counts starts and cancels separately. A true observer draws sparse authoritative frames and presents each authoritative kick once on its watch clock. Speculative flashes are reversible cosmetics; this policy does not promise that audio already played can be undone.

The network gate starts a dedicated authority, striker, spiker and true observer at 240 ms injected gameplay RTT. It requires two accepted spikes, local spike Godot-node displacement over 12 game pixels within four ticks and before acknowledgement, predicted kicks, matching 0–1 score/winner, the ball reset to center everywhere, and reconciled kick-event counts. RSB_METRICS reports application bytes, replayed ticks and ball correction magnitudes (including disagreements around predicted resets). These values are initial diagnostics, not CPU percentiles or a Kit/Replay comparison.

Session/UI acceptance#

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/ui_run.sh

The host, player and observer use real ENet sessions with 120 ms receive delay per process. The gate checks validated names, host-only start, literal chat, input capture, held scores/ping, departure and rejoin. It drives the actual scene signals and keyboard action map; separate native captures also exercise Space activation of the menu and rendered score overlays.

The content ID is now 0x5253504545444234. Name/start state and commands changed its initial schema in revision 2; revision 3 also changes the manual-start rule: the first connected seat leads the match. A planned network handoff preserves that leader, while a disconnected leader yields to the first surviving seat. Revision 4 adds a match round counter and round-scoped restart command. No implicit old-archive conversion is claimed.

Native host migration#

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/migration_run.sh

This three-member local fixture exercises planned handoff and abrupt host loss through the existing Replay Room driver and SQLite coordinator. A successor prepares the complete pitch, including player identity, score and moving ball. Recovery advances the authority epoch, restores that checkpoint, reconnects the survivors and resumes commands, chat and presentation. The authority's Handoff button requests a freeze/release; the recovery label shows progress and the known rollback distance. Reconnecting clients reinstall their cosmetic event policy and clear correction smoothing associated with the old epoch.

The fixture enables Room with RSB_COORD_PORT, RSB_MEMBER (1–3), RSB_INCARNATION and a 64-character hexadecimal RSB_COORD_KEY. Its coordinator uses room 49, localhost endpoints and fixed development credentials. Members 1 and 2 can host; member 3 exercises a peer without checkpoint capability. Without these Room settings, the normal Solo/Host/Join/Watch flows use direct sessions. This remains a fixed migration fixture. The separate party menu now uses durable enrollment and invites through a configured room service.

Use a fresh RSB_MIGRATION_OUT directory to retain evidence. Set RSB_MIGRATION_MODES=planned to select one scenario, or RSB_MIGRATION_RENDER=1 for native windows and recovery screenshots. Each scenario requires an exactly restored moving checkpoint with a nonzero score, two new accepted spikes, new-epoch chat and matching canonical worlds among survivors. The gate applies 120 ms receive delay per game process; it does not simulate raw packet loss. Manual match-leader succession additionally has a pure-model test; lobby migration and consecutive failures need separate end-to-end coverage.

Play again and local profiles#

After a match ends, the first connected seat can press Play again. The command requires the current round number and enough connected players, and rejects stale requests, guests and observers. It resets ball/kickoff, player motion/cooldowns, score and per-match counters while retaining names, seats, connections and match settings. Authority epochs and the session's action sequence continue. Presentation cuts to the new pitch, the button hides, and chat announces the new match.

Native play stores reconnect identity at user://replay_speedball_identity and the name at the same path plus .name, independently of the original game's profile. Set RSB_PROFILE to another path for each local player/process. Its parent directory must exist. RSB_NAME overrides the initially displayed name; a successful connection persists the chosen value. RSB_PERSIST=0 opts into temporary identity/name handling. An explicit RSB_TOKEN uses test credentials and bypasses profile reads and writes. Malformed or unwritable profiles produce a visible error before joining; existing identity is never silently replaced. Browser play uses IndexedDB through the existing identity/name adapters; connection controls wait for the initial profile read. A fresh browser process is tested below. Native files and browser storage remain separate backends.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/round_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/profile_run.sh

The round gate uses a host, player and observer at 120 ms receive delay each. It plays two complete matches, rejects guest restart, checks cleared totals and retained seats/names, and exchanges chat after the second match. RSB_ROUND_RENDER=1 runs native windows and captures the winner's Play again button. The profile gate kills a client and starts another process with its files, requiring the same seat and name; it also checks malformed-file preservation and explicit-token precedence. Both launchers accept fresh output directories (RSB_ROUND_OUT, RSB_PROFILE_OUT).

Original Speedball's boot helper already persisted reconnect identity. Its game scripts do not expose Play again or a match save/load menu. Restart and saved display names are Replay additions. The native save/resume front door is described below.

Save and resume a pitch#

Direct native hosts and solo players can click Save · F5 or press F5 outside chat. The menu's Save file field chooses the destination (RSB_SAVE supplies its default, user://speedball.replay). Its parent directory must exist. A successful save records the complete authority checkpoint, including the scored/moving pitch, round, roster and command frontiers. The latest completed save replaces the selected slot through the existing staging-file/rename helper. A failed write preserves the previous archive and reports an error.

From the menu, Resume solo restores offline play; Resume host opens the restored pitch for friends. Use the same local profile that saved the game. Another participant's profile, a damaged/missing file or incompatible content cannot open that archive as a player host. Scripted authority launches can use RSB_RESUME=1. A dedicated archive must be resumed with the server role; the visible buttons are for player-hosted saves.

Resume advances the saved authority epoch, restores the exact frame, retires accepted-but-unexecuted commands, and disconnects remote seats until they rejoin. Fresh clients use normal Join/Watch; an opt-in, credential-free query of the chosen direct host learns its current epoch before the regular handshake. Friends retain their own profiles and reclaim their seats. Local chat scrollback is not part of a match file. Manual file resume assumes the old runtime has stopped; it is separate from automatic host migration and does not elect/fence competing hosts.

Room-managed games keep their coordinator recovery path; manual file saving and resume are disabled for them. Browser solo saves use named IndexedDB slots, described below. No old schema conversion or power-loss durability guarantee is added by this UI.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/save_run.sh

The gate saves a scored, moving pitch, kills both peers, tests solo restore and wrong-owner/damaged/missing-file rejection, then starts fresh host/client processes. It requires exact frame equality, the same seats/names, new spikes, a completed match, restart into round 2 and chat. It also blocks a second staging write and verifies that the previous archive survives. Set a fresh RSB_SAVE_OUT to keep artifacts, and RSB_SAVE_RENDER=1 for native menu/resume captures.

Browser parties#

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/online_web_run.sh

The Web export uses the same scene, pitch and Party/Room flow. Browser launch settings use lowercase query keys without the RSB_ prefix: room_service, room_local, players, goals, latency, name and persist, for example. Browser multiplayer uses a configured party service and WebRTC; raw direct ENet joins remain native. Personal identity and display name use the replay-speedball IndexedDB namespace, while room credentials use replay-speedball-rooms. Profile reads finish before connection controls become active; corrupted/unavailable storage reports an error rather than silently switching identity.

The browser gate runs a host, player and true observer in separate Chrome profiles. It verifies actual RTC traffic, planned handoff and host loss, an exact scored/moving checkpoint, observer leave/rejoin and a fresh browser process returning with the same personal identity, display name, invite and seat. New spikes/chat must precede matching canonical worlds. RSB_WEB_OUT selects a fresh artifact directory; RSB_WEB_MODES=planned narrows the scenarios. The default runner builds and exports; verified prebuilt runs require an existing matching Web export.

The test uses local HTTP/WS with explicit development mode and 120 ms application receive delay. Host loss closes the host browser without handoff. It does not establish public HTTPS/WSS deployment, TURN-only routing, raw packet-loss behavior, OS process-kill durability, other browser engines or human play-feel parity. Browser solo saves are described below. Party evidence and screenshots.

Browser solo save slots#

In the browser's local menu, Save slot chooses a name and Resume solo opens its checkpoint. Names contain 1–48 letters, numbers, dots, dashes or underscores; save_slot selects the initial name (default pitch). Slots are scoped to the persistent personal identity and stored in the replay-speedball IndexedDB namespace. Local files and browser slots are separate backends.

During solo play, Save/F5 captures once while the game continues. Saving… means the write was submitted; Saved match… appears only after the completed IndexedDB receipt. Reload resumes the exact checkpoint at a newer epoch with the normal pending-command retirement policy. Saving again replaces the slot only if its observed revision is still current. A stale tab reports a conflict and keeps the newer archive; it does not refresh merely to force an overwrite.

A damaged slot cannot be resumed or overwritten. New solo play remains available, and after Leave you can choose another slot. An unreadable/corrupt personal identity blocks connection without replacement. Browser Solo can save even when a party service is configured, but slot selection/resume uses the local menu configuration. Leased Room matches continue to use coordinator recovery and cannot be saved through this solo flow.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/browser_save_run.sh

The gate kills the owned Chrome process with SIGKILL after a completed save, resumes with the same identity/name and exact scored/moving frame, executes new spikes, finishes/restarts the match and saves round 2. It then exercises competing tabs, corrupt archives, alternate slots and corrupt identity records, checking that the previous data remains unchanged. RSB_BROWSER_SAVE_OUT selects a fresh artifact directory. This is local Chrome process-crash evidence; power-loss durability, browser eviction/private modes and other browser engines remain separate requirements. Room save publication and abandoned-party restoration now use the distinct party recovery flow. Solo-slot evidence.
